entries.title: Canvas writes return 422 while reads succeed (missing or invalid CSRF token)
entries.root_cause: Verified live 2026-09-22: Canvas returns exactly this generic body when a non-GET request arrives without a valid X-CSRF-Token. Reproduced on demand with absent header and with deliberately wrong token, byte-identical bodies. The most likely probe-side cause is harvesting the token from the csrf-token meta tag, which the tenant homepage currently does not have (verified live), so the header is never sent.
entries.is_not: This is not Canvas blocking writes, not rate limiting (rate-limit headers showed a full bucket, no 429s, no Retry-After), not session death (a dead session 302s API calls instead of 422), not a write halt (write_halt_active was false), and not a tenant-side change (tenant changes return 401 or 403 with specific messages, and writes work again with zero config changes once the token is sent).
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried {operation} on {tenant}, and every write came back with an HTTP 422 (unprocessable_content) while reads kept working fine. What the evidence showed: your sign-in is healthy and the rate limit is untouched, so this is not a broken session. Canvas is asking for a security token (X-CSRF-Token) that the request did not carry, which is the standard missing-or-invalid-token response, reproduced exactly with absent and wrong tokens. What this means: your Canvas session is fine and nothing on your side changed; the request just needs to carry a fresh token, which the normal write path fetches automatically on each call. What happens next: I am resending through the normal page-context path, which fetches a fresh token per call, and verifying with a readback.
entries.auto_action: Retry the write through the canonical page-context path with a fresh _csrf_token cookie harvest per call, then run a terminal readback to confirm the write landed.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate only if the canonical path also 422s with a confirmed token harvest, and include the x-request-context-id so it can go to Instructure; that combination was never observed in the audit.
entries.signature_notes: affects: "every non-GET regardless of encoding (JSON, form-encoded, PUT, UI route)"; body_contains: "unprocessable_content"; http_status: 422; rate_limit_remaining: ">0 (bucket full, e.g. 700.0)"; reads_ok: true; retry_after_header: "absent"; session_health: "logged_in=true, keepalive healthy"; writes_fail: true

entries.title: Write refused before sending: no _csrf_token in the live browser session
entries.root_cause: The page-context write path harvests the X-CSRF-Token fresh from the _csrf_token cookie on every call. When the live document.cookie has no _csrf_token (helper tab navigated away, cookie expired, or session otherwise degraded), the write is refused before any network call. This is the fail-closed fix for the 2026-09-22 incident where missing tokens produced misleading provider 422s; the product path can no longer produce a silent missing-token write.
entries.is_not: This is not a provider refusal: no HTTP request was sent, so there is no 422 and nothing was applied. It is not session death either (a dead session redirects API calls to the login page); it is specifically the CSRF cookie missing from a live page.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: Morrow stopped before sending the change, because the Canvas page the helper keeps open could not confirm that the change came from your signed-in session (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: nothing was sent and nothing changed. The helper page may be open on another page, or your sign-in may need a refresh. What happens next: I will check that you are still signed in on the helper page. Then say the word and I will prepare the change again; in plan mode you approve it again before it is sent.
entries.auto_action: Probe the helper /status; if it reports logged_in false, guide the educator to sign in again on the helper page. Nothing was sent and the executor never resends on its own: prepare the change again (plan-write, or catalog in edit mode) only after the educator says so. Never build a CSRF header by hand.
entries.escalate_when: the helper session is healthy and the tenant tab is open but document.cookie still has no _csrf_token
entries.signature_notes: fail-closed pre-send refusal raised by transport/local_chromium.py (CsrfTokenMissing; transport/chromium_session.py raises it for a write as CsrfWriteNotSent, a WriteNotAttempted) or transport/browser_backend.py (BrowserCsrfTokenMissing); no provider contact happened

entries.title: Canvas write returned HTTP 422 unprocessable_content (probable CSRF token problem)
entries.root_cause: Canvas returns this generic 422 body when a non-GET request arrives without a valid X-CSRF-Token (verified live 2026-09-22 with absent and wrong tokens, byte-identical bodies). It can also be a genuine validation error on the payload. Without the full write/read/session evidence the two cannot be distinguished from status and body alone.
entries.is_not: This is not proven to be a CSRF problem from this evidence alone; it is also not proven to be session death (dead sessions 302 API calls to the login page instead of 422) or rate limiting (that surfaces as 429).
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: Canvas refused the change without saying why (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: nothing changed in Canvas. Most often the Canvas page the helper keeps open needs a refresh, but Canvas may also have refused a value. What happens next: I will check that you are still signed in on the helper page. Then say the word and I will prepare the change again; if Canvas refuses it again, I will tell you and we can change what we send.
entries.auto_action: Probe the helper /status; if it reports logged_in false, guide a fresh sign-in on the helper page. Nothing was saved and the executor never resends on its own: prepare the change again (plan-write, or catalog in edit mode) only after the educator says so. If Canvas refuses the same change twice, report it and stop.
entries.escalate_when: the canonical path also 422s with a confirmed fresh token harvest
entries.signature_notes: hedged variant: matches on status plus body alone, so a bare 422 dict or a ProviderHttpError carrying the body still gets a CSRF-aware message. The strict canvas-csrf-422-writes-only entry (8 predicates) wins by specificity when the full writes_fail/reads_ok/session evidence is present.

entries.title: Canvas did not accept a value in the change, so nothing changed
entries.root_cause: Canvas answers a write it will not save with HTTP 400 or 422 and an errors body that names the field and the reason (for example {"errors": {"title": [{"message": "is too long"}]}}). The executor fails fast on a 4xx: Canvas refused the request, so nothing was saved, and the op id is released for a new attempt.
entries.is_not: This is not a missing security token (that 422 carries unprocessable_content and has its own mode), not session death, and not a change that might have applied.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: Canvas did not accept this change and said: {validation_messages} (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: nothing changed in Canvas. What happens next: I can fix the value and ask you to approve the change again.
entries.auto_action: Tell the educator what Canvas said, correct the value, run plan-write again, and ask for a new approval; never resend the same request
entries.escalate_when: never; Canvas refused a value and nothing changed
entries.signature_notes: classification: "ProviderHttpError on a write"; fixed_behavior: "fail fast on 4xx, nothing saved, op id released"; triggers: ["a 400 or 422 whose body carries an errors list or map"]; not: ["the CSRF 422 (unprocessable_content)"]

entries.title: Canvas 429 rate limiting
entries.root_cause: Verified mechanism: Canvas's rate limiter answered 429 with the bucket exhausted. Distinguishing evidence from the 422-CSRF failure: the 429 carries x-rate-limit-remaining at 0.0 and a Retry-After header, while the CSRF 422 carries a full bucket (700.0) and no Retry-After.
entries.is_not: This is not a write block, not a CSRF problem, and not session death. The tiebreaker against the 422 CSRF mode: check x-rate-limit-remaining and the presence of Retry-After before classifying.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried {operation} on {tenant} and Canvas answered 429, its polite way of saying too many requests at once. What the evidence showed: the rate-limit bucket at zero and a Retry-After instruction, so this is confirmed throttling, not a broken session or a blocked write. What this means: the request is valid but needs to wait its turn. What happens next: I am honoring Canvas's Retry-After and retrying automatically; writes that were in flight are recorded as uncertain and I will verify with a readback before reporting success.
entries.auto_action: Backoff for the Retry-After duration and retry. Reads retry up to 4 times; writes convert to UncertainWrite and get reconciled by readback.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate if 429s persist across several backoff cycles on low-volume traffic, which would suggest a tenant-side policy change rather than normal throttling.
entries.signature_notes: http_status: 429; rate_limit_remaining: "0.0"; reads_behavior: "retried up to 4 times then fail"; retry_after_header: "present (honored)"; writes_behavior: "become UncertainWrite immediately, Retry-After honored"

entries.title: Canvas says this account may not do this, so nothing changed
entries.root_cause: Canvas answers 401 with status "unauthorized" ("user not authorized to perform that action") or 403 when the signed-in account's role in the course, or its permissions, do not allow the request, for example a TA changing a course setting only a teacher can change. The session is live: an expired session answers 401 "unauthenticated", which is session death. The executor fails fast on a 4xx: Canvas refused the request, nothing was saved, and the op id is released.
entries.is_not: This is not an expired sign-in (a 401 "unauthenticated" is session death), not a problem with the values in the request, and not a change that might have applied.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: Canvas says your account does not have permission to do this (status {status_code}), and said: {validation_messages} (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: nothing changed in Canvas. Your role in this course, or your school's Canvas settings, do not allow this for your account. What happens next: I will not try it again. If you should be able to do this, check that Morrow is signed in to your own Canvas account, or ask the course's teacher or your Canvas admin about your role.
entries.auto_action: Tell the educator what Canvas said and that nothing changed; do not retry; if they believe their account should be allowed, suggest checking the signed-in account and their course role with the teacher or Canvas admin
entries.escalate_when: never; Canvas refused the request for this account and nothing changed
entries.signature_notes: classification: "ProviderHttpError the executor classified as fail-fast (it sets operation_kind)"; fixed_behavior: "fail fast on 4xx, nothing saved, op id released"; triggers: ["401 unauthorized", "403"]; not: ["401 unauthenticated (session death)"]

entries.title: Canvas could not find the item, so nothing changed
entries.root_cause: Canvas answers 404 when the course, page, assignment, or other item in the request does not exist at that address: it was deleted, its address changed (a renamed page gets a new address), or the id is wrong. The executor fails fast on a 4xx: nothing was saved, and the op id is released.
entries.is_not: This is not an expired sign-in, not a permission refusal, and not a change that might have applied.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: Canvas could not find it (status 404), and said: {validation_messages} (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: nothing changed in Canvas. The item may have been deleted or renamed, or the course or item number is wrong. What happens next: I can look the item up again in the course and try again with what I find. A change still needs your approval first.
entries.auto_action: Tell the educator nothing changed; list that kind of item in the course again to find its current id or address (a renamed page has a new address), then prepare the request again; never resend the same request
entries.escalate_when: never; Canvas found nothing at that address and nothing changed
entries.signature_notes: classification: "ProviderHttpError the executor classified as fail-fast (it sets operation_kind)"; fixed_behavior: "fail fast on 4xx, nothing saved, op id released"; triggers: ["404"]

entries.title: Canvas refused the request, so nothing changed
entries.root_cause: Canvas answered a 4xx status that no more specific mode covers, for example 409 (a conflicting change) or 413 (a request too large), or a 400 or 422 with no reason in the body. The executor fails fast on a 4xx: Canvas refused the request, nothing was saved, and the op id is released.
entries.is_not: This is not a change that might have applied: the executor classified the refusal as fail-fast. It is not the missing security token either (that 422 carries unprocessable_content and has its own mode).
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: Canvas refused the request (status {status_code}), and said: {validation_messages} (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: nothing changed in Canvas. What happens next: I will not send the same request again. I can check the item and the values, then try again with a corrected request. A change still needs your approval first.
entries.auto_action: Tell the educator what Canvas said and that nothing changed; do not resend the same request; read the target again and correct the request before trying again
entries.escalate_when: never; Canvas refused the request and nothing changed
entries.signature_notes: classification: "ProviderHttpError the executor classified as fail-fast (it sets operation_kind)"; fixed_behavior: "fail fast on 4xx, nothing saved, op id released"; the more specific Canvas modes (validation refusal, rate limit, not permitted, not found) come first in this file, so they win a tie

entries.title: Canvas session died (login page returned, SessionDead)
entries.root_cause: Verified mechanism: the provider's session cookie expired, was revoked, or the SSO flow lapsed, so the tenant answers with its login page (redirect or HTTP 200 HTML). The transport detects both shapes and raises SessionDead. Expiry is never warned ahead of time: the keepalive watches process health and the URL heuristic, never the expiry horizon (known real horizons included a stay-signed-in credential expiring 2026-10-05 and an OTP remember-me expiring 2026-10-21), so the first signal is a failed op.
entries.is_not: This is not a write block and not rate limiting. A dead Chromium masquerades similarly but shows url='' with logged_in=false and needs a browser restart, not a sign-in.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: Morrow could not use your Canvas sign-in on the helper page: Canvas asked for a sign-in, or the helper's browser stopped (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: nothing about the task itself went wrong, and nothing more goes to Canvas until your sign-in works again. A change that was under way is set aside, not lost. What happens next: I will check the helper page. If it asks you to sign in, sign in there again; I will check that it is still your account, then ask you before anything that was set aside runs again.
entries.auto_action: The executor already paused writes and set aside the in-flight change. Probe the helper /status: if the helper or its browser is down, restart it with helper/keepalive.sh; if it reports logged_in false, guide the educator to sign in again on the helper page, then run reauth/state_machine.py resume, which checks the account. Nothing set aside runs again without the educator's approval.
entries.escalate_when: Always bring this to the educator: only they can re-sign in, and only they can approve the resume of quarantined ops.
entries.signature_notes: http_status_variants: ["302 to /login", "200 with login HTML in body (content sniff raises SessionDead)"]; reads_behavior: "fail as SessionDead; pre-hardening reads journaled the login page as success"; status_endpoint: "logged_in=false"; writes_behavior: "UncertainWrite if a write was attempted, otherwise nothing journaled"

entries.title: Session died mid-write, effect state unknown (UncertainWrite)
entries.root_cause: Verified mechanism: the session died between dispatch and the provider's answer, so the transport cannot prove whether Canvas applied the write. The write-integrity hardening (wave 2) classifies this as UncertainWrite rather than retrying blindly, which would risk a double-apply.
entries.is_not: This is not a confirmed failure and not a confirmed success. Treating it as either is how silent double-applies happened before the hardening.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried {operation} on {tenant} and the session died right in the middle of the write, so I cannot tell from the transport alone whether Canvas applied it. What the evidence showed: an UncertainWrite record in the journal with the attempt details kept, which is the honest classification the system uses instead of guessing. What this means: the write may or may not have landed, and retrying blindly could create a duplicate. What happens next: I am running a terminal readback against Canvas to see whether the object exists as written; if it did not land, I will re-dispatch under a fresh claim, and if it did, I will report it done with the evidence.
entries.auto_action: Reconcile via terminal readback (member GET, list readback). If the write did not land, re-dispatch only after the session is healthy; never retry the ambiguous write blindly.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate if the readback cannot decide the state (provider gives no listable signal), so the educator can check the object in the Canvas UI before any re-dispatch.
entries.signature_notes: classification: "UncertainWrite"; journal: "audit record journaled under a fresh event id with the step evidence retained"; verify_path: "terminal readback (list the object, read the member GET) decides applied vs not-applied"

entries.title: Typo'd, placeholder, or unreachable tenant shows a Canvas error page
entries.root_cause: Verified live in the new-user audit: the logged_in heuristic was URL-based and returned true on Canvas error pages and chrome-error pages, so a typo'd or unreachable tenant looked signed in. The fix requires the tab URL to start with the tenant base and excludes error titles.
entries.is_not: This is not a session problem and not provider throttling. Signing in cannot fix a wrong tenant.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried to reach {tenant} and what loaded is a Canvas error page, not your login. What the evidence showed: the error title in the tab and a URL that does not match your school's Canvas address, so the address itself is wrong, unreachable, or a placeholder that was never replaced. What this means: no sign-in can help until the Canvas address is correct. What happens next: I am not attempting any operations against this address; please confirm the exact Canvas URL for your school and I will re-probe it before doing anything else.
entries.auto_action: Refuse all dispatch against the bad tenant; re-probe the tenant root after the educator supplies the corrected base and gate onboarding on a real authenticated signal (users/self succeeding).
entries.escalate_when: Always: only the educator can supply the correct tenant address.
entries.signature_notes: error_titles: ["Oops, Canvas can't find your login page", "chromewebdata error"]; probe_rule: "url must start with the configured tenant base; error titles excluded"; status_endpoint: "url is a Canvas error page or chrome-error page"

entries.title: Canvas soft-delete: DELETE returns 200 but the object still reads back 200
entries.root_cause: Verified live 2026-09-22 on a classic quiz: Canvas returned 200 to two DELETEs and direct GET still returned 200 afterward, yet the quiz was absent from the course listing (66 listed), its backing assignment 404d, and its questions list was empty. This is provider-side soft-delete behavior, not a failed delete.
entries.is_not: This is not a failed deletion and not a permission problem. Re-issuing DELETEs does not help.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I deleted {object} on {tenant} and Canvas confirmed with a 200, but a direct fetch of the object still returns 200. What the evidence showed: the object is gone from the course listing, its backing assignment returns 404, and its questions list is empty, which is Canvas's soft-delete behavior on this object type: functionally deleted in every user-visible sense while the direct fetch still answers. What this means: the delete worked and no further action is needed. What happens next: I am recording the absence evidence in the receipt and moving on rather than re-issuing the delete.
entries.auto_action: Accept the deletion after verifying absence through the course listing, the backing assignment, and the questions list. Do not re-issue the DELETE.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate only if the object is still user-visible (in the course listing or functional), which would indicate the delete genuinely did not take.
entries.signature_notes: absence_evidence: "object absent from the course listing, backing assignment 404s, questions list empty"; delete_status: 200; terminal_get: "200 (object still readable)"

entries.title: Stale read right after delete (immediate GET still 200, later 404)
entries.root_cause: Verified live: provider read replicas served a stale object immediately after deletion; the delete was effective.
entries.is_not: This is not a failed delete and not soft-delete. Waiting or re-reading settles it.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I deleted {object} on {tenant} and the immediate verification fetch still returned it. What the evidence showed: its read replicas can serve the old copy for a short window after a real delete: on the live battery the same pattern resolved to 404 minutes later. What this means: the delete is very likely fine and the verification read raced the provider's consistency. What happens next: I am re-inspecting after a short delay rather than re-deleting; if it resolves to 404, the delete is proven.
entries.auto_action: Wait and re-read once after a short delay. Only re-issue the delete if the object remains present after the delay.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate if the object is still present after several minutes, which would suggest a genuine delete failure rather than replica lag.
entries.signature_notes: evidence_note: "live-proof 2026-09-22: module item immediate post-delete GET returned 200, re-inspection minutes later returned 404"; immediate_terminal_get: "200"; later_terminal_get: "404"

entries.title: Classic quiz GET with include[]=questions returns 200 with 0 embedded questions
entries.root_cause: Verified live 2026-09-22 on this tenant: the include param does not embed questions here; the dedicated questions endpoint is the working read path.
entries.is_not: This is not a read failure and does not mean the quiz has no questions.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I read {object} on {tenant} asking Canvas to embed its questions, and it came back with none. What the evidence showed: the request succeeded (200) but this tenant simply does not embed questions on that route; the dedicated questions endpoint for the same quiz returned all of them. What this means: the quiz is intact and the embed parameter is the wrong tool here. What happens next: I am fetching questions through the dedicated endpoint and treating that as the read path.
entries.auto_action: Fall back to the dedicated questions endpoint; do not treat the empty embed as a failed read.
entries.escalate_when: No escalation; this is a routine tenant-shape quirk, handled automatically.
entries.signature_notes: dedicated_endpoint: "questions endpoint returns all questions (26 observed)"; request: "GET quiz with include[]=questions"; response: "200, 0 embedded questions"

entries.title: Collection counts landing on exactly 100 (per_page cap)
entries.root_cause: Verified live: Canvas caps page size at 100 per_page; the Chromium lane now follows valid Link: rel=next headers. Pre-fix, the lane returned only one page with no partial-results warning.
entries.is_not: This is not the true total.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I listed {collection} on {tenant} and got exactly 100 items. What the evidence showed: 100 is Canvas's per-page cap, not necessarily the real total, and I saw this exact pattern on the live battery. What this means: the list may be incomplete. What happens next: I am paging through the Link headers (or re-requesting with per_page=100) to get the full set before I summarize anything.
entries.auto_action: Follow Link rel=next pagination to completion; never report a 100-count as a total.
entries.escalate_when: No escalation; pagination is handled automatically.

entries.title: Tenant-side write behavior change (course lock, enrollment loss)
entries.root_cause: Hypothesis, documented as the investigated alternative in the 2026-09-22 write-block investigation: tenant admin actions such as course locking or enrollment loss return 401 or 403 with specific messages. Ruled out in that incident because writes work now with zero config changes; kept as a live mode because the signature is distinct.
entries.is_not: This is not the CSRF 422 (different status and body), not throttling, and not session death.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried {operation} on {tenant} and Canvas refused with a {status_code} and a specific message rather than its generic error body. What the evidence showed: it points at a change on the tenant side, such as the course being locked or your enrollment changing, not at anything wrong with the request. What this means: the provider is enforcing a policy that a retry cannot satisfy. What happens next: I am not retrying; I need you to check the course's lock or enrollment state with your Canvas admin, and I will re-attempt once that is resolved.
entries.auto_action: Do not retry; record the provider message verbatim and park the op.
entries.escalate_when: Always: resolving a course lock or enrollment change needs the educator or their Canvas admin.

entries.title: Item Bank canonical item DELETE returns provider 404
entries.root_cause: Verified live: the provider 404s the canonical direct item DELETE. Entry-level delete (IB-7, entry DELETE 204 with terminal list readback) is the proven removal path; deleting entries and archiving the bank is the terminal pattern.
entries.is_not: This is not a permissions failure and not a product bug; the route is unserved.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: I tried to delete the item through the direct item route and Canvas answered 404. What the evidence showed: the provider does not serve item-level deletes on this route, while entry-level deletes and bank archiving work and are the proven cleanup pattern. What this means: the item cannot be deleted that way, but the working alternative achieves the same end. What happens next: I am deleting at the entry level (with a terminal list readback proving the absence) and archiving the bank if that was the intent.
entries.auto_action: Delete via the entry DELETE route with list-absence proof, then archive the bank; keep IB-19 pending.

entries.root_cause: Verified live: the provider refuses the bank-link call with 401. Documented as provider-unserved, consistent with the Item Bank scope-policy pattern.

entries.root_cause: Verified mechanism: the executor runs a saved multi-step task (execute --entry) or its undo only when pack/pack.json pins that entry with a matching sha256. This release pins no entry, so every such run is refused before anything is sent (a changed entry file is refused the same way).

This version has no automatic undo. What happens next: to reverse a change, I can prepare the opposite change as a new change, and in plan mode I will show it to you for approval first.

An argument that is not valid JSON, or not the shape the command takes, is refused before anything is sent. --body takes a JSON object, or a JSON array of objects for the bulk date update.

What the evidence showed: Morrow checked the request before sending it, and part of it was not in a form Morrow accepts, so it stopped before sending anything to Canvas (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: nothing was sent and nothing changed. What happens next: I will correct the request and run it again.
entries.auto_action: Read engineering_detail for the argument that was refused, correct it, and run the command again. Nothing was sent, so the retry is safe.
entries.escalate_when: Never on its own: the refusal is a local input check. Escalate only if a correct argument is refused.

With no terminal to ask on (an agent run) and no --yes, the executor refuses before doing anything.

What the evidence showed: this step changes Morrow's own records, so it runs only when the command includes --yes, and it was run without it (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: nothing ran and nothing changed. What happens next: finish the steps that come before it in the recovery instructions, then run the same command again with --yes added.

entries.escalate_when: Never on its own: the refusal is a confirmation check. Escalate only if the command with --yes fails.

entries.title: Helper server not running
entries.root_cause: Verified: the helper is supervised every 5 minutes, by a cron entry where the machine has cron, or by the keepalive background loop (helper/supervisor.py) where it does not (the Muse VM has no cron daemon). After a restart the helper stays down until that supervision runs keepalive; on a machine without cron the background loop starts again only with `bin/morrow start` or the next morrow command.
entries.is_not: This is not session death; there is no browser to check yet.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: the helper, the private browser Morrow uses to reach Canvas on your Muse computer, is not running (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: your Canvas sign-in is not affected, and nothing was sent. What happens next: I will start the helper again and check that you are still signed in, then try again.
entries.auto_action: Run helper/keepalive.sh to relaunch, then run bin/morrow start so supervision keeps it up (it starts the keepalive background loop on a machine without cron and is a no-op with cron), then re-probe /status and session health.
entries.escalate_when: Escalate if the helper fails to come up after keepalive recovery (log the real failure from server.log), since a human may need to re-sign in.
entries.signature_notes: evidence: transport/chromium_session.py _ensure_transport raises ExecutorError('chromium backend: browser unavailable (...); the login helper endpoint is down too -- start it with helper/keepalive.sh, then retry') when the browser launch fails and the helper /status endpoint is unreachable. Previous signature keyed on 'helper_reachable', which no production code ever sets, so the entry could never match (2026-09-22 first-run audit). ChromiumSession.raw_request raises it as HelperNotReached (a WriteNotAttempted: nothing was sent) with the same text.

For a change, say the word and I will prepare the change again; in plan mode you approve it again before it is sent.

Nothing was sent and the executor never resends on its own: prepare a change again (plan-write, or catalog in edit mode) only after the educator says so.

entries.title: A different Canvas account is signed in to the helper
entries.root_cause: Verified mechanism: before every write, and once per session for reads, the Chromium lane reads GET /api/v1/users/self and compares it with the account pinned at first sign-in (reauth/state_machine.py pin). Someone signed in to the helper browser as another account (a shared machine, a second educator, a student), so the lane refused and imposed the re-auth write halt.
entries.is_not: This is not an expired session and not a permission error on one course. The other account's identity is never shown.
entries.agent_message: What was attempted: {operation}. What the evidence showed: the helper page is signed in to a different Canvas account than the one you confirmed when you set up Morrow (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: nothing was sent, and changes are paused so nothing goes out under the wrong account. What happens next: sign out on the helper page (Account, then Logout) and sign back in with your own account; I will check that it is the account you confirmed and continue. To use a different account from now on, I can disconnect Morrow first so you can sign in fresh.
entries.auto_action: Keep the write halt. After the educator signs back in, run reauth/state_machine.py resume, which verifies the live account against the pin; to change accounts, run bin/morrow disconnect with the educator's yes, then sign in and pin again.
entries.escalate_when: Always: only the educator can sign back in as their own account or choose to disconnect.
entries.signature_notes: evidence: transport/chromium_session.py ChromiumSession._verify_principal raises PrincipalMismatch when GET /api/v1/users/self differs from reauth/state_machine.pinned_principal() (final muse audit M3).

entries.title: No Canvas account is pinned, so a write cannot prove who it runs as

What this means: nothing was sent, and Morrow makes no change until you confirm that the signed-in account is yours. What happens next: I will read the name of the account signed in on the helper page and ask you to confirm it is you, then try again.
entries.auto_action: Run reauth/state_machine.py pin --first-signin, show the educator the printed name and get their confirmation; when the pin record is damaged, disconnect (with the educator's yes) and sign in fresh.
entries.escalate_when: Always: the educator must confirm the account is theirs.
entries.signature_notes: evidence: transport/chromium_session.py ChromiumSession._verify_principal raises PrincipalNotPinned for a write with no pin, or for any call when pinned_principal() raises PrincipalPinError (final muse audit M3).

That read failed or returned no account id (for example HTTP 500), so the lane refused before sending the request.

What the evidence showed: before sending anything, Morrow checks which Canvas account is signed in on the helper page, and Canvas did not answer that check (reference {correlation_id}). What this means: Morrow did not send the request, so nothing was sent and nothing changed. What happens next: I will check that the helper page shows you signed in to Canvas, then try a read again. For a change, say the word and I will prepare the change again; in plan mode you approve it again before it is sent.
